scales.name: Threat reactivity
scales.definition: How readily and how durably negative emotion is triggered by threat, loss or criticism.

facets.name: Trigger threshold
facets.definition: How little it takes to set off negative emotion.

facets.name: Persistence
facets.definition: How long negative emotion lasts once triggered.

facets.name: Anticipation
facets.definition: How much is spent on threats that have not happened.

bodyLinks.mechanism: Cortical 5-HT2A binding tracks the inward facets of neuroticism (r = .37, replicated with a second tracer), and SSRIs lower neuroticism beyond their effect on depression.
bodyLinks.verification: No individual-level test. Group-level PET and drug-response evidence only.

items.text: Small criticisms land harder on me than they should.
items.informantText: Small criticisms land harder on them than they should.

review.notes: Re-tagged mild → moderate: the item asks the respondent to concede disproportion, which is a stronger admission than a mild-band statement.

items.text: It takes a lot to rattle me.
items.informantText: It takes a lot to rattle them.

review.notes: Stoicism is differently valued by culture and gender; the same inner experience may be reported differently. DIF-test by gender.

items.text: I pick up on a change in someone's tone straight away.
items.informantText: They pick up on a change in someone's tone straight away.

review.notes: Boundary with A7 detail/change sensitivity, and with sensory processing sensitivity generally. Detection is not the same as distress; cut if it loads on A7.

items.text: People describe me as hard to upset.
items.informantText: People describe them as hard to upset.

items.text: A short, neutral message from someone can put me on edge.
items.informantText: A short, neutral message from someone can put them on edge.

items.text: I can be corrected in front of other people without it getting to me.
items.informantText: They can be corrected in front of other people without it getting to them.

review.notes: Face and public correction carry different weight across cultures; flagged for DIF by locale.

items.text: The smallest sign of disapproval can change how my whole day feels.
items.informantText: The smallest sign of disapproval can change how their whole day feels.

items.text: Things that visibly upset other people genuinely don't sting me.
items.informantText: Things that visibly upset other people genuinely don't sting them.

review.notes: Extreme low-pole item. Risks capturing emotional flatness or callousness rather than low reactivity; check cross-loading on A5 callousness and on the state block.

items.text: Something that went wrong hours ago is still running in my head.
items.informantText: Something that went wrong hours ago is still running in their head.

items.text: Once a difficult conversation ends, I stop thinking about it.
items.informantText: Once a difficult conversation ends, they stop thinking about it.

review.notes: Reworded from "Once a difficult conversation is over, it's over for me", which readers found ambiguous — "it's over" could be heard as the relationship ending rather than the rumination stopping. The construct is persistence, so the replacement names the mental act directly. Item is still status:draft, so the id is reused rather than retired.

items.text: I replay conversations looking for what I should have said.
items.informantText: They replay conversations looking for what they should have said.

items.text: I let go of things faster than most people I know.
items.informantText: They let go of things faster than most people they know.

items.text: A single piece of criticism can stay with me for days.
items.informantText: A single piece of criticism can stay with them for days.

items.text: I can set a worry aside and come back to it when it's useful.
items.informantText: They can set a worry aside and come back to it when it's useful.

items.text: I've lost nights of sleep over something someone said in passing.
items.informantText: They've lost nights of sleep over something someone said in passing.

review.notes: Sleep content overlaps the Block C insomnia and Block B sleep-reactivity material. The anchor here is the trigger (a passing remark), not the sleep loss; verify it doesn't load on the state block.

items.text: Even after a serious setback, I'm back to myself within a day.
items.informantText: Even after a serious setback, they're back to themselves within a day.

review.notes: Extreme low-pole item with high desirability — resilience is flattering. Matched by p01/p05 at the opposite pole; drop if desirability correlation is strong in Pilot 1.

items.text: I plan around things going wrong.
items.informantText: They plan around things going wrong.

review.notes: Boundary with conscientious planning. The anticipation facet is about threat expectancy, not organization; watch for cross-loading on A3 follow-through.

items.text: My mind stays on what's in front of me rather than what might go wrong.
items.informantText: Their mind stays on what's in front of them rather than what might go wrong.

review.notes: Reworded to remove a negation: agreeing with "I don't ..." makes the disagree side a double negative, which is a known source of respondent error. The pole and keying are unchanged; only the phrasing is now a positive assertion of the same thing.

items.text: Before something important, I rehearse how it could go badly.
items.informantText: Before something important, they rehearse how it could go badly.

items.text: I deal with problems when they arrive rather than before.
items.informantText: They deal with problems when they arrive rather than before.

review.notes: Re-tagged moderate → mild: dealing with problems as they arrive is an ordinary preference, not a marked absence of anticipation.

items.text: I notice myself bracing for bad news that hasn't come.
items.informantText: They brace for bad news that hasn't come.

items.text: Waiting on a result I can't control doesn't particularly bother me.
items.informantText: Waiting on a result they can't control doesn't particularly bother them.

items.text: I've turned down chances I wanted because of what might go wrong.
items.informantText: They've turned down chances they wanted because of what might go wrong.

review.notes: Deliberate near-pair with a1_drive_f11 ('let opportunities go because it looked like too much work'). Same behavior, different motive: threat vs effort cost. If the two correlate above .60 the motive distinction isn't reaching respondents and one must go.

items.text: I can walk into a situation with an uncertain outcome feeling no dread at all.
items.informantText: They can walk into a situation with an uncertain outcome feeling no dread at all.

citations.title: The association between brain serotonin 2A receptor binding and neuroticism in healthy individuals: a Cimbi database independent replication study
citations.claim: Cortical 5-HT2A binding is associated with the inward facets of neuroticism (r = .37) in an independent replication.

citations.title: Personality change during depression treatment: a placebo-controlled trial
citations.claim: Paroxetine reduced neuroticism 6.8x as much as placebo among patients matched for depression improvement.
